newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania private bank at odds with shareholder.
newsitem.headline: Romania private bank at odds with shareholder.

text.p: The major shareholder in Romania's Banca de Credit Cooperatist Bankcoop SA on Monday defended himself against accusations from the bank president that he was seeking to take control.
George Paunescu, a prominent businessman, issued a statement saying attacks against him were "an attempt to cover bad management at the bank".

At an impromptu news conference late on Sunday, Bankcoop president Alexandru Dinulescu said Paunescu, who holds 44 percent of Bankcoop's capital, was putting pressure on the bank and seeking to take control.

Dinulescu said he had asked the central National Bank of Romania bank (BNR) to launch an inquiry into Paunescu's aquisition of Banckoop shares. BNR officials could not immediately confirm any investigation.

In 1995 Bankcoop fought off local market and media speculation alleging problems at the bank. Later that year Paunescu, head of a large media and tourism holding and an influential figure on Romania's emerging markets, acquired $10 million worth of Bankcoop shares.

The row with Paunescu came after Bankcoop reported an end-1996 balance sheet of 2.1 trillion lei ($480.5 million) at end-1996, 870 billion lei up from 1995 and a 1996 gross profit of 66 billion ($15.1 million).

Over the past year problems at two private banks -- Renasterea Creditului Romanesc Credit Bank SA and Dacia Felix SA -- undermined confidence in the banking sector, which is still dominated by state-owned banks. ($=4,370 lei)
